category_specific_evidence: Reproducer: multipletests([]) raises ZeroDivisionError: float division by zero, while fdrcorrection([]) returns (array([], dtype=bool), array([], dtype=float64))
Root cause: alphacSidak and alphacBonf are computed from 1 / ntests before method dispatch, so an empty pvals array fails for every method
Fix: guard with ntests > 0; otherwise alphacSidak and alphacBonf are set to np.nan and per-method branches run on the empty array
Regression test test_multipletests_empty parametrized over methods asserts reject and pvals_corrected have shape (0,) and that alphac_sidak and alphac_bonf are nan via np.isnan
Passages describe the failure as an exception on empty input, not a numeric discrepancy at a dtype or tolerance; the dtype and tolerance fields are not stated in any passage
reproduction_risks: Passages do not state any dtype or floating-point precision the discrepancy depends on; the reproducer uses an untyped empty list
Passages do not give a tolerance at which correct and incorrect answers separate; the regression test uses exact shape and isnan checks only, with no rtol or atol
Large p-value arrays in the test diffs are fixture data and do not establish a magnitude regime for the bug
The PR date is blank in the known-instance record, so no version or date can be grounded
Reproducing the bug requires only an empty input, so the defect is not a 1-ULP-scale effect and no default-tolerance masking is evidenced
